A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same R2PS work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison, including the new Appendix D.3 in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original pursuit-evasion simulations, policy-training curves, capture success rates, inference timings and ablation results in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds larger-pursuer-team success rates and computational scaling results in Appendix D.3.

M1.justification: Appendix D.3 introduces a larger-team adaptation using EPG’s grouping mechanism to derive pursuer and evader policies. The central DP algorithm, belief updates, SAC objective and GNN architecture remain unchanged; the grouping procedure is only briefly described.

E1.justification: The training corpus and test maps are unchanged. Appendix D.3 extends evaluation from two pursuers to four- and six-pursuer scenarios on the existing maps, modestly expanding the tested multi-agent environments.

E2.justification: The shortest-path, DPPos, DPbelief and PSRO comparisons retain their membership. The added larger-team evaluation tests R2PS against the asynchronous DP evader without adding a competing pursuer baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix D.3 adds a team-size sweep over m = 2, 4 and 6 with observation range fixed at 2, and reports inference FLOPs across graph sizes and team sizes. Previously reported training budgets, evaluation horizon and other settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Table 8 tests sensitivity of capture success to pursuer-team size, while Figure 7 examines computational scaling with graph size and team size. Existing observation-range, belief-update, policy-guidance and graph-size analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The existing description of averaging success rates over 500 tests is unchanged. v2 adds no seed counts, repeated-training information, confidence intervals or statistical tests; the new displays introduce no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results in Tables 1–4 and 6–7 and the original plotted results are unchanged. Table 8 adds larger-team outcomes: Hollywood Walk of Fame retains 0.38 for two pursuers and reports 0.82 and 0.93 for four and six pursuers. Figure 7 adds FLOPs results across team and graph sizes.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 corrects an induction step from V*(s) = gamma^k to gamma^(k−1), fixes the referenced induction direction and state notation, and revises the queue-order contradiction. Appendix A.2 corrects the enqueued object from a distance value to a state. The theorem statements remain unchanged; renaming Lemma 2 as Proposition 1 adds no theoretical content.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions retain the same scope: asynchronous DP optimality, belief-based pursuit under partial observability, and robust real-time cross-graph generalization outperforming PSRO. Shortened introduction and conclusion passages do not substantively redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 adds a substantive explanation that policy guidance helps avoid trivial responses to equilibrium opponents, illustrated with Rock-Paper-Scissors, and distinguishes transitive weakness from dominance. Section 2.1 also drops its stated rationale of avoiding inherent PSPACE-hardness through the chosen formulation.

D1.justification: A new footnote in Section 4.2 supplies a code-repository location, absent from v1. Existing architecture, hyperparameter, hardware and graph-processing details are retained. The larger-team grouping experiments receive no detailed implementation or training recipe.

R1.justification: v2 adds a citation to Lu et al. (2025c) on equilibrium learning and bibliography entries for Chai et al. (2025) and Zhao et al. (2026). Appendix D.3 additionally credits EPG’s grouping mechanism. The paper’s central positioning relative to EPG and prior pursuit-evasion research remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 shortens parts of the introduction and conclusion, rewrites the Section 4.1 motivation, corrects wording and updates author information and acknowledgments. The main section and appendix organization is retained, with one additional experimental subsection.

P2.justification: The manuscript is reformatted throughout into the ICLR layout, changing the title block, recurring headers, text width, heading typography and float placement. Figure 3 changes from three columns by two rows to two columns by three rows, and Table 8 and Figure 7 are added. Existing figure content and table structures are otherwise largely retained.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful larger-team scalability evidence in Appendix D.3, corrects local mathematical errors in Appendix A.1 and supplies a code-access pointer. These strengthen empirical support and documentation while preserving the original findings. The new grouping setup remains only briefly described, so the overall quality gain is limited.
